subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — post-call recap

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary:
- You wanted confirmation on what we persist in request/response logs (headers, body, trace ids) and how we support redaction/masking of PII.
- You also asked about retention windows, region/residency options, and how our defaults interact with Dedicated/Private deployments.

What Redwood can do (high level):
- Request/response logs: by default we capture minimal request metadata for debugging (timestamps, request size, model id, short latency traces). Request and response bodies are configurable — customers can opt-in to full request/response logging for a specific route.
- Headers & trace IDs: we store routing metadata (route id, region, trace id) for scalable observability; trace ids are redacted in exported logs by default for hosted accounts but can be retained for Dedicated/Private when requested under contract.
- PII/sensitive redaction: we support configurable redaction rules (regex-based masks, token-level PII detectors, and custom scrubbers). These run at ingestion and before any persisted logs are written.
- Retention & residency: retention is configurable per-account and per-route; hosted defaults are 30 days, Dedicated/Private can set custom retention and data residency (region selection + VPC).

Requested next steps:
1) I attached a one-page overview of our logging controls and a mapping template to capture your specific logging needs. Please fill the template with the fields you want retained vs redacted and share back.
2) Rishi and I will prepare answers for your security questionnaire items about redaction tooling and retention SLAs (SOC2 evidence where applicable).
3) If you want, we can schedule a short technical deep-dive next week to walk through sample logs and masking behavior.

Is Wednesday or Thursday morning (PST) better for the deep-dive?

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf (1 page)
- fintech-mapping-template.xlsx (spreadsheet template)
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FintechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Engineering <eng@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from the security/engineering side: 

1) Trace IDs: can you confirm whether trace IDs are stored with any request/response payloads, or only in a separate routing metadata table? We need to understand linkability for incident forensics.

2) Headers: will you strip Authorization-like headers and any custom headers that may contain tokens by default? If not, can we configure header-level allowlists/denylists?

3) Redaction latency: for regex-based and token-detector redaction, is redaction synchronous at write time (i.e., blocking), or async (logs can be briefly available before redaction)? We need guarantees for short retention exposures.

4) Retention policy: hosted default of 30 days is fine for initial POC, but for production we will likely need 90 days for certain telemetry. Can Redwood support per-route 90d retention in Dedicated?

We filled the mapping template (attached) with our fields; one open item is sample logs so we can validate the redaction rules. Could you provide redacted examples and a short walkthrough?

—Alice
Sr. Product Security Manager
FintechCo
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — internal notes

Marissa — forwarding to capture our internal next steps. Notes: 
- Trace IDs: hosted accounts redact trace ids in exported logs by default; however, we persist ephemeral trace mapping for live debugging (TTLed). For Dedicated/Private, customers can keep full trace ids under contract and put that data into their VPC. Need to confirm SLA language for incidence forensics.
- Headers: we have header allowlist/denylist at the gateway; Authorization and cookie-like headers are stripped from persisted logs unless explicitly allowlisted by the customer. Default denylist includes common auth headers.
- Redaction latency: regex/token detectors run synchronously in the ingestion pipeline before write to persisted logs for hosted; we still need to confirm for very high throughput routes whether async batching could surface brief windows. Flag to infra to confirm pipeline guarantees.
- Retention: Dedicated supports per-route retention policy via config; 90d is feasible. Need to confirm pricing impact and legal sign-off for data retention windows.

Action items (internal):
1) Rishi to confirm synchronous redaction guarantees and provide short blurb for SOC2 evidence.
2) Marissa to send sample redacted logs and schedule deep-dive.

Rishi
From: FintechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>

Hi Marissa, Alice —

Thanks for the template. We redacted the template and highlighted three priority fields: account_number, user_email, and session_token. For validation we need:

- Two pairs of sample request/response logs: one with PII present (to test redaction rules) and one with only metadata (to validate that we do not lose observability). Please redact anything beyond the three fields above in your samples before sending.
- A short explanation of how trace ids are stored and whether they can be correlated to raw payloads for Dedicated vs hosted.
- Confirmation that header allowlist/denylist is configurable and the default denylist includes Authorization, Cookie, and X-Auth-* headers.

We are OK with a redacted PDF sample plus a short recording for the deep-dive.

Regards,
FintechCo Security Team
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction — sample logs request

Hi — attaching two redacted sample log PDFs and a link to a short demo recording. Highlights: 

- Samples included: sample-1-redacted.pdf (request contains PII, redacted via regex + ML detector), sample-2-metadata-only.pdf (routing/latency/debug metadata only).
- Trace ids: hosted: trace ids are stored in an internal routing layer with short TTL and are redacted in exported logs by default; Dedicated/Private: customers may choose to retain full trace ids in their VPC. We will include a short paragraph for your security questionnaire.
- Headers: default denylist strips Authorization, Cookie, and X-Auth-*; customers can manage custom allow/deny lists via the Console or API.
- Redaction guarantees: ingestion pipeline performs synchronous inspection and redaction before write for hosted accounts — we confirmed with infra that there is no window where raw PII is persisted. I attached the infra confirmation note (excerpt) in the overview PDF.

Next steps: 
- I scheduled a 45-minute deep-dive for Thu 2026-07-16 09:00 PT. Invite sent separately.
- Please confirm the mapping template fields and any additional logs you'd like us to include in the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
